project.name: exchange-server2
project.description: Single-instrument limit order book in Java 17 with a price-time matching engine, a checksummed write-ahead journal with deterministic replay and snapshots, and a single-writer thread model behind an authenticated TCP/TLS gateway.

nodes.name: CancelResult.java
nodes.summary: Immutable record describing the outcome of a cancel (status, order id, cancelled quantity), with validation and factory methods; an unknown order is a normal return value, not an exception (D17).
nodes.languageNotes: Java record with a compact canonical constructor that enforces invariants between status and quantity.

nodes.name: CancelResult
nodes.summary: Record of a cancel outcome with invariant checks and cancelled()/unknown() factories.

nodes.name: CancelStatus.java
nodes.summary: Enum of cancel outcomes: CANCELLED or UNKNOWN_ORDER, where not owning an order deliberately maps to UNKNOWN_ORDER (D48).

nodes.name: CancelStatus
nodes.summary: Enum: CANCELLED or UNKNOWN_ORDER.

nodes.name: LevelUpdate.java
nodes.summary: Record for level-2 market data: the side, price, total volume and order count of one price level after a command; volume 0 means the level is gone.

nodes.name: LevelUpdate
nodes.summary: Record of one price level's side, price, volume and order count after a command.

nodes.name: ExchangeClient.java
nodes.summary: Minimal blocking client for the line protocol used by ClientMain and the gateway tests; a background reader thread queues lines and await() finds matching lines while keeping skipped ones for later lookups.

nodes.name: ExchangeClient
nodes.summary: AutoCloseable socket client with a background reader queue and predicate-based waits that keep skipped lines.

nodes.name: OutputDigest.java
nodes.summary: Running FNV-1a 64 digest over a canonical, field-by-field text encoding of every engine output (D70), written into journal CHECK records so replay divergence after a behaviour change is detected.
nodes.languageNotes: Encodes fields explicitly instead of relying on toString()/hashCode(), whose formats Java does not guarantee.

nodes.name: OutputDigest
nodes.summary: Package-private FNV-1a 64 running digest of engine outputs, resumable from its hex form.

nodes.name: OutputListener.java
nodes.summary: Functional interface invoked on the writer thread with each command's engine output and numbered private events, before the request future completes (D76); implemented by the gateway and never called during replay.

nodes.name: OutputListener
nodes.summary: Functional interface with onOutput(EngineOutput, List<PrivateEvent>) and a no-op NONE instance.

nodes.name: OutputLog.java
nodes.summary: Numbers each participant's private events (oseq) deterministically from engine outputs and retains the most recent ones per participant to serve RESEND requests (D73); can resume numbering from a snapshot.

nodes.name: OutputLog
nodes.summary: Package-private per-participant event numbering and bounded retention store for RESEND.

nodes.name: PrivateEvent.java
nodes.summary: Sealed interface for a participant's private stream messages (D73): OrderReply, CancelReply and MakerFill records, each numbered per participant so replay rebuilds identical oseq numbering.
nodes.languageNotes: Sealed interface with nested record permits, enabling exhaustive pattern matching.

nodes.name: PrivateEvent
nodes.summary: Sealed interface over OrderReply, CancelReply and MakerFill private stream records.

nodes.name: CancelAllOutput.java
nodes.summary: Engine output record for a CANCEL_ALL (D72): one CANCELLED result per removed order in book priority order plus the resulting level updates; never contains trades or fills.

nodes.name: CancelAllOutput
nodes.summary: EngineOutput record for a CANCEL_ALL with per-order cancel results.

nodes.name: CancelOutput.java
nodes.summary: Engine output record for a single cancel command: the CancelResult and level updates, with empty trade and passive-fill lists.

nodes.name: CancelOutput
nodes.summary: EngineOutput record for a single cancel.

nodes.name: EngineOutput.java
nodes.summary: Sealed interface for everything one command produced: sequence number, timestamp, trades, passive fills and level updates, separating private results from public market data.

nodes.name: EngineOutput
nodes.summary: Sealed interface permitting OrderOutput, CancelOutput and CancelAllOutput.

nodes.name: cancelled
nodes.summary: Factory for a CANCELLED result with the order id and removed quantity.

nodes.name: unknown
nodes.summary: Factory for an UNKNOWN_ORDER result with zero quantity.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Writes one protocol line to the server and flushes it.

nodes.name: await
nodes.summary: Returns the first line matching a predicate within a timeout, searching previously skipped lines first and keeping new non-matching lines for later.

nodes.name: awaitPrefix
nodes.summary: Convenience wait for the first line starting with a given prefix.

nodes.name: linesUntil
nodes.summary: Collects lines up to and including one matching a predicate, within a timeout.

nodes.name: nextLine
nodes.summary: Takes the next unseen line from the incoming queue within a timeout.

nodes.name: isClosedByServer
nodes.summary: Reports whether the server closed the connection (EOF reached) within a timeout.

nodes.name: readLoop
nodes.summary: Background reader loop that pushes each received line, then an EOF marker, onto the incoming queue.

nodes.name: field
nodes.summary: Static helper extracting a key=value field from a server line.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the client socket.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Folds one engine output into the digest by encoding its sequence, timestamp, response, trades, fills, cancel results and level updates field by field.

nodes.name: record
nodes.summary: Turns one command's engine output into numbered private events (requester reply first, then maker fills) and retains them; throws on a mismatched command/output pair.

nodes.name: since
nodes.summary: Returns a participant's retained events from a given oseq onward for RESEND, or signals a gap if they are no longer retained.

nodes.name: trades
nodes.summary: Returns an empty list: a CANCEL_ALL never trades.

nodes.name: passiveFills
nodes.summary: Returns an empty list: a CANCEL_ALL produces no fills.

nodes.name: trades
nodes.summary: Returns an empty list: a cancel never trades.

nodes.name: passiveFills
nodes.summary: Returns an empty list: a cancel produces no fills.

nodes.name: Execution.java
nodes.summary: Record for a fill on a resting (passive) order addressed to its owner, the only way the maker learns about its fills.

nodes.name: Execution
nodes.summary: Record of a passive fill delivered to the resting order's owner.

nodes.name: OrderOutput.java
nodes.summary: Engine output record for a new order: the Response (whose trades are exposed as the output's trades), passive fills and level updates.

nodes.name: OrderOutput
nodes.summary: EngineOutput record for a new order, delegating trades to its Response.

nodes.name: Reason.java
nodes.summary: Enum of state-dependent reasons a new order did not simply trade and rest (duplicate client order id, price band, open-order and book caps, post-only cross, self-trade prevention), with isReject() distinguishing rejects from SELF_TRADE_PREVENTED cancels.

nodes.name: Reason
nodes.summary: Enum of engine reject/cancel reasons with isReject().

nodes.name: Trade.java
nodes.summary: Validated record of one trade: resting-level price, quantity, both order ids, aggressor side and the incoming command's timestamp (D34, keeps replay deterministic).

nodes.name: Trade
nodes.summary: Validated trade record with positive price and quantity.

nodes.name: Protocol.java
nodes.summary: Defines and implements the ASCII line wire protocol (D53): parses client messages (LOGIN, NEW, CANCEL, RESEND, SUBSCRIBE, ...) and formats server lines (FILL, ORDER, CANCELLED, BOOK, TRADE, LEVEL, ERROR); its header comment is the protocol reference.

nodes.name: Protocol
nodes.summary: Non-instantiable utility class with static parse and format methods for the line protocol.

nodes.name: TcpGateway.java
nodes.summary: Thread-per-connection TCP/TLS gateway that accepts sessions, authenticates logins, enforces session limits (D74, D75) and, as the exchange's OutputListener, routes private events to the participant's sessions and market data to subscribers; triggers cancel-on-disconnect.
nodes.languageNotes: Nested Settings record uses immutable with-er methods; session sets use ConcurrentHashMap compute for atomic add/remove per key.

nodes.name: TcpGateway
nodes.summary: Gateway class implementing OutputListener: accept loop, session registry, routing and settings.

nodes.summary: Unit tests for OutputDigest: identical outputs give identical digests, every output kind and every field contributes, cancel results are included, and the digest resumes from its hex form.

nodes.name: OutputDigestTest
nodes.summary: JUnit test class for OutputDigest.

nodes.name: OutputLogTest.java
nodes.summary: Unit tests for OutputLog: per-participant oseq numbering with requester first, CANCEL_ALL numbering, retention limits, resume after snapshot, and rejecting a mismatched command/output pair.

nodes.name: OutputLogTest
nodes.summary: JUnit test class for OutputLog.

nodes.name: ProtocolTest.java
nodes.summary: Unit tests for Protocol grouped into Parse and Format: parsing valid and malformed client lines and formatting every server line type.

nodes.name: ProtocolTest
nodes.summary: JUnit test class with @Nested Parse and Format groups.

nodes.name: TcpGatewayTest.java
nodes.summary: End-to-end gateway tests over real sockets using ExchangeClient and a journalled ExchangeService, grouped into Session, Security, Limits, Trading, Resend, CancelOnDisconnect and MarketData behaviours, including restart persistence.

nodes.name: TcpGatewayTest
nodes.summary: JUnit integration test class with seven @Nested behaviour groups and start/stop/login helpers.

nodes.name: trades
nodes.summary: Returns the trades carried by the order's Response.

nodes.name: isReject
nodes.summary: True for every reason except SELF_TRADE_PREVENTED, which pairs with CANCELLED rather than REJECTED.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Parses one client line into a ClientMessage (LOGIN, NEW, CANCEL, RESEND, SUBSCRIBE, PING, QUIT, ...), enforcing arity and line length.

nodes.name: parseNew
nodes.summary: Parses the fields of a NEW order line, handling MARKET orders without a price.

nodes.name: lines
nodes.summary: Formats a private event as protocol lines: FILL/ORDER for order replies, CANCELLED or CANCEL_REJECT for cancels, a MAKER FILL for passive fills, optionally marked resend=1.

nodes.name: levels
nodes.summary: Formats book levels as price x qty lists for BOOK snapshots, using '-' for an empty side.

nodes.name: port
nodes.summary: Returns the bound local port.

nodes.name: startAccepting
nodes.summary: Starts the daemon acceptor thread; fails if already accepting.

nodes.name: attach
nodes.summary: Attaches the ExchangeService that sessions forward requests to.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Attaches the service and starts accepting in one step.

nodes.name: acceptLoop
nodes.summary: Accept loop with exponential backoff on transient failures, a session cap that answers ERROR, and creation of a ClientSession per connection.

nodes.name: removed
nodes.summary: Unregisters a closed session and, when it was the participant's last and requested COD, issues a journalled CANCEL_ALL (D72).

nodes.name: onOutput
nodes.summary: Writer-thread callback that formats private events for each session of the participant and TRADE/LEVEL lines for subscribers, only enqueuing lines so no client can stall the exchange.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the server socket and drops every session without stopping the exchange.

nodes.name: eachFieldChangesTheDigest
nodes.summary: Checks that changing any single field of an output changes the digest.

nodes.name: itResumesFromItsHexForm
nodes.summary: Checks that a digest resumed from its hex string continues identically.

nodes.name: eachParticipantIsNumberedFromOneRequesterFirst
nodes.summary: Checks per-participant numbering starting at 1 with the requester's reply ahead of maker fills.

nodes.name: onlyTheMostRecentEventsAreRetained
nodes.summary: Checks that only the last `retention` events are kept and older RESEND requests report a gap.

nodes.name: resumingContinuesTheNumberingWithNothingRetained
nodes.summary: Checks that resume() continues oseq numbering from snapshot values with no retained events.

nodes.name: credentials
nodes.summary: Builds low-iteration test Credentials for the participants used by the tests.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts a journalled ExchangeService and TcpGateway with given settings for a test.

nodes.name: restartKeepsTheBookForTheNextGateway
nodes.summary: Checks that restarting the exchange from its journal preserves the book for a new gateway.

nodes.name: ExchangeException.java
nodes.summary: Defines the runtime exception callers receive when a request gets no business result, with a Reason enum (BUSY, STOPPED, HALTED, INTERNAL_ERROR) that tells them whether to retry, resend, or give up.

nodes.name: ExchangeException
nodes.summary: RuntimeException carrying a Reason code so callers can distinguish queue backpressure, shutdown, writer halt, and quarantined engine failures (D49, D51).

nodes.name: ExchangeService.java
nodes.summary: Implements the single-writer thread model: any caller thread hands requests into one queue, and the dedicated 'exchange-writer' thread drains them in smart batches (or linger group-commit) and calls Exchange.process, journalling with one fsync per batch. Manages the RUNNING/STOPPING/STOPPED/HALTED lifecycle under one lock so no accepted request is ever lost.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CompletableFuture hand-off (whenCompleteAsync) so callers never receive the writer's own future, and a stop-marker sentinel compared by identity to end the drain loop.

nodes.name: ExchangeService
nodes.summary: Owns the exchange-writer thread and the request queue; exposes future-based and callback-based submit/cancel/snapshot/cancelAll/attach/resend, enforces queue capacity under a lock, and halts cleanly on journal or writer failure.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Static factory that opens the Exchange (journal recovery included) and starts the writer thread with the given settings and output listener.

nodes.name: submit
nodes.summary: Hands a new OrderRequest to the writer queue, returning a caller-owned future of the Response or invoking a callback on the writer thread (gateway variant).

nodes.name: cancel
nodes.summary: Queues a cancel of one order for a participant, completing with a CancelResult via future or callback.

nodes.name: snapshot
nodes.summary: Queues a book snapshot read of the given depth so it observes state between earlier and later requests.

nodes.name: cancelAll
nodes.summary: Queues a cancel-all for a participant, completing with the list of cancel results in book priority order (D72).

nodes.name: resend
nodes.summary: Queues a read of the participant's retained private events from a given output sequence number (D73).

nodes.name: attach
nodes.summary: Callback variant that registers a session on the writer thread and reports the participant's latest output sequence number, so the private stream joins without a gap (D73).

nodes.name: handOff
nodes.summary: Copies the writer-completed internal future into a fresh caller-owned future completed asynchronously, so caller continuations or cancellation cannot stall or influence the writer (D61).

nodes.name: enqueue
nodes.summary: Checks state and capacity and enqueues a pending request under the shared lock, refusing with a STOPPED, HALTED or BUSY ExchangeException when it cannot be accepted.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Flips the state to STOPPING and enqueues the stop marker under the lock, then waits up to a timeout for the writer to drain and close the journal.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: The writer thread loop: take one request, drain up to maxBatchSize, optionally linger, process the batch through Exchange, track batching stats, and close the journal as its last act.

nodes.name: linger
nodes.summary: Group-commit mode: keeps polling for more requests until the batch is full or the linger deadline passes; kept only for benchmark comparison.

nodes.name: halt
nodes.summary: Marks the service HALTED, records the cause, and fails every request in the current batch and the remaining queue with a HALTED ExchangeException.

nodes.name: Request.java
nodes.summary: Sealed interface of records describing what a caller hands to the writer queue before stamping: Submit, Cancel, CancelAll (journalled commands) and Snapshot, Attach, Resend (unjournalled reads), each typed by its result.
nodes.languageNotes: Java 17 sealed interface with a generic result type parameter and compact record constructors that validate on the caller's thread.

nodes.name: Request
nodes.summary: Package-private sealed request hierarchy whose type parameter R is the result each request completes with; compact constructors reject bad depth/oseq before reaching the writer thread.

nodes.name: ResendResult.java
nodes.summary: Record answering a RESEND request with retained private events, the first still-retained output sequence number, and the participant's latest one (D73).

nodes.name: ResendResult
nodes.summary: Immutable record of resent private events plus firstAvailable and lastOseq, letting the gateway detect gaps the exchange cannot fill.

nodes.name: OrderRequest.java
nodes.summary: Immutable client order before stamping and the only stateless validation layer (D19): checks participant and client order id patterns, quantity and price limits from Rules, and that market orders carry no price. Reused by the gateway and the journal decoder.

nodes.name: OrderRequest
nodes.summary: Value class with a private validating constructor and typed factories (limit, ioc, fok, postOnly, market, of) so the in-memory no-price sentinel never leaks to callers.

nodes.name: of
nodes.summary: General factory taking an OptionalLong price: requires it absent for MARKET and present for every other type, then delegates to the validating constructor.

nodes.name: limit
nodes.summary: Convenience factory for a priced limit order.

nodes.name: market
nodes.summary: Convenience factory for an unpriced market order using the NO_PRICE sentinel internally.

nodes.name: equals
nodes.summary: Value equality over all six order fields.

nodes.name: BookSnapshot.java
nodes.summary: Record of the book as of a command: last processed sequence number, last trade price, and best-first bid/ask level lists that a market-data subscriber starts from.

nodes.name: BookSnapshot
nodes.summary: Immutable book snapshot record with defensively copied bid and ask LevelUpdate lists.

nodes.name: OrderStatus.java
nodes.summary: Enum of the four outcomes of a new order (FILLED, RESTED, CANCELLED, REJECTED), each implying a different next action for the client (D23).

nodes.name: OrderStatus
nodes.summary: Order outcome enum used by Response and the wire protocol.

nodes.name: Response.java
nodes.summary: Record telling a submitter the result of a new order (D22): order id, status, reason, filled/remaining quantities and own trades, with a constructor that enforces consistency invariants so engine bugs fail before reaching a client.
nodes.languageNotes: Compact record constructor used as an invariant checker: trades must sum to filledQuantity and status/reason combinations are cross-checked with a switch statement over the enum.

nodes.name: Response
nodes.summary: Immutable order response whose compact constructor validates that trades sum to the filled quantity and that status, reason and remaining quantity cannot contradict each other.

nodes.name: ClientSession.java
nodes.summary: One TCP client connection with a reader thread (parse, LOGIN authentication, stateless checks, in-flight cap and token-bucket rate limit) and a sender thread draining a bounded outbound queue; closes only after every handed-in request completes (D74-D76).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a String sentinel created with new String() and compared by identity, AtomicInteger in-flight tracking, and volatile fields for cross-thread handoff between reader, sender and the exchange writer.

nodes.name: ClientSession
nodes.summary: Package-private per-connection session that bridges protocol lines to ExchangeService calls and never blocks the writer thread when sending (slow clients are disconnected, D54).

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Non-blocking offer of an outbound line to the bounded queue, called from the writer thread; disconnects the client if the queue is full.

nodes.name: readLoop
nodes.summary: Reader thread body: reads lines with timeouts, dispatches them to handle, and marks the reader done so the session can close once in-flight requests finish.

nodes.name: readLine
nodes.summary: Reads one line from the socket with a maximum length, signalling overlong input so the session can refuse it.

nodes.name: handle
nodes.summary: Dispatches one parsed client message: PING, QUIT, LOGIN, then (after login and admission checks) NEW, CANCEL, RESEND, SUBSCRIBE and UNSUBSCRIBE to the ExchangeService.

nodes.name: admit
nodes.summary: Applies the per-session in-flight cap and token-bucket rate limit, returning SESSION_BUSY or RATE_LIMITED when a request must be refused (D75).

nodes.name: login
nodes.summary: Handles LOGIN with one attempt per connection: validates the participant pattern, authenticates the secret, sets the idle timeout and cancel-on-disconnect, and attaches to the participant's stream before sending WELCOME (D73, D74).

nodes.name: newOrder
nodes.summary: Builds an OrderRequest from a NEW message (reporting validation errors as ERROR) and submits it to the service, replying only on refusal.

nodes.name: resend
nodes.summary: Requests retained private events from an output sequence number, replying RESEND_GAP when the start is no longer retained, else sending each event's lines.

nodes.name: subscribe
nodes.summary: Starts a market-data subscription: requests a book snapshot on the writer thread, sends it, and registers the session for level updates, guarding races with a subscription lock.

nodes.name: tracked
nodes.summary: Wraps a completion callback to count in-flight requests and close the session after the last one completes (D76).

nodes.name: sendLoop
nodes.summary: Sender thread body: drains the outbound queue to the socket until the close sentinel arrives, then closes the socket.

nodes.summary: Benchmark operation: submits one limit order alternating sides at one price and blocks on the response future.

nodes.name: SequencerTest
nodes.summary: JUnit test class with @Nested groups Stamping, InvalidInputUsesUpNothing, Clock, Resume and CommandValidation.

nodes.summary: Concurrent tests of ExchangeService: hand-in, stop semantics, backpressure, writer failures, batching and robustness, using a Gate CommandInterceptor to block the writer deterministically.

nodes.name: ExchangeServiceTest
nodes.summary: JUnit test class with @Nested groups HandIn, Stop, Backpressure, Failures, Batching and Robustness plus a Gate interceptor test seam.

nodes.name: ExchangeTest.java
nodes.summary: Tests the Exchange facade: live path, restart and recovery, poison-pill quarantine, CHECK checkpoints, compaction to snapshots, and operations.

nodes.name: ExchangeTest
nodes.summary: JUnit test class with @Nested groups LivePath, Restart, PoisonPill, Checkpoints, Compaction and Operations over temp-dir journals.

nodes.name: interceptorSeesEveryCommandLiveInOrder
nodes.summary: Verifies the CommandInterceptor seam observes every stamped command on the live path in sequence order.

nodes.name: MutableClock.java
nodes.summary: Thread-safe test Clock that can be set or advanced (including backwards), shared by sequencer, exchange and service tests to control timestamps deterministically.

nodes.name: MutableClock
nodes.summary: java.time.Clock subclass backed by a volatile Instant, fixed to UTC.

nodes.name: at
nodes.summary: Factory creating a MutableClock at a parsed ISO-8601 instant.

nodes.name: advance
nodes.summary: Synchronised move of the clock forward or backward by a Duration.

nodes.name: set
nodes.summary: Sets the clock to an absolute instant.

nodes.name: OrderBook.java
nodes.summary: Owns the lifecycle of every resting order: bid/ask TreeMaps of PriceLevels plus an id map and per-participant open counts, with all mutations funneled through add, fillBest and cancel so the book invariants hold in one place.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a reverse-ordered TreeMap for bids and a LinkedHashSet of touched levels so drained level updates come out in deterministic order.

nodes.name: OrderNode.java
nodes.summary: Package-private doubly linked list node holding an Order inside a PriceLevel; a null order marks a sentinel, enforced by construction.

nodes.name: PriceLevel.java
nodes.summary: Time-priority queue of orders at one price on one side, implemented as a sentinel-bounded doubly linked list; public read-only state, package-private mutators so only OrderBook can change it.

nodes.name: CancelAllCommand.java
nodes.summary: Journalled command record that cancels every resting order of one participant (cancel-on-disconnect, D72), validating sequence number and participant in its compact constructor.
nodes.languageNotes: Java record with a compact canonical constructor used for invariant checks.

nodes.name: CancelOrderCommand.java
nodes.summary: Journalled command record that cancels one resting order by its exchange order id, validating sequence number, participant and target id.

nodes.name: Ledger.java
nodes.summary: Writer-thread-owned bundle of everything derived from commands (matching engine, output digest, per-participant output log), built from a snapshot and rebuilt as one unit on poison-pill recovery.

nodes.name: OrderBook

nodes.name: cancel

nodes.name: removeNode

nodes.name: drainLevelUpdates

nodes.name: restingOrders

nodes.name: ordersAt
nodes.summary: Package-private test seam returning orders at a level and verifying forward and backward links agree.

nodes.name: checkInvariants
nodes.summary: Package-private test seam that verifies all book invariants: id map vs levels, no empty or crossed levels, level totals and open counts.

nodes.name: OrderNode
nodes.summary: Linked list node with prev/next pointers and owning level; sentinels created only via sentinel().

nodes.name: PriceLevel
nodes.summary: Price level holding a sentinel-bounded FIFO of orders with cached total volume and order count.

nodes.name: addOrder
nodes.summary: Package-private append of an order at the tail of the level, checking side, price and duplicate linkage.

nodes.name: fillHead
nodes.summary: Package-private fill of the head order by a quantity, updating total volume while leaving unlinking to OrderBook.

nodes.name: unlink
nodes.summary: Package-private O(1) unlink of a node from the level, adjusting volume and order count.

nodes.name: CancelAllCommand
nodes.summary: Record command carrying sequence number, timestamp and participant for a cancel-all.

nodes.name: CancelOrderCommand
nodes.summary: Record command carrying sequence number, timestamp, participant and target order id.

nodes.name: Ledger
nodes.summary: Package-private holder of engine, digest and output log that applies commands and produces snapshots.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Dispatches a command to the matching engine by type, updates the output digest and records numbered private events.

nodes.name: Order.java
nodes.summary: Accepted order domain object: a validated OrderRequest plus sequencer-issued id and timestamp, tracking filled and remaining quantity with no knowledge of where it is stored.

nodes.name: MatchingBenchmark.java
nodes.summary: JMH benchmark measuring best-level lookup, rest-and-take and add-and-cancel costs of the engine at 10, 1000 and 100000 price levels per side.

nodes.name: OrderBookTest.java
nodes.summary: JUnit tests for OrderBook organised in @Nested groups (add, fillBest, cancel, open orders, level updates, walk) plus an invariant check under randomized traffic.

nodes.name: MatchingEngineTest.java
nodes.summary: Extensive JUnit suite for MatchingEngine covering limit, IOC, FOK, market and post-only orders, cancels, risk bands, self-trade prevention, caps, cancel-all, snapshots, outputs, guards and determinism.

nodes.name: Order
nodes.summary: Accepted order with immutable identity fields and mutable filled quantity.

nodes.name: Order
nodes.summary: Constructor building an Order from a validated OrderRequest, checking only the id and timestamp.

nodes.name: fill
nodes.summary: Increases the filled quantity, rejecting non-positive or over-remaining fills.

nodes.name: Rules

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README: ExchangeServer2 is a crash-safe, deterministic, single-instrument exchange in Java 17, with price-time matching, a checksummed write-ahead journal with replay and snapshots, a single-writer thread model and an authenticated TCP/TLS gateway. Its diagram shows the path you will follow in this tour: client, gateway, queue, writer thread (stamp, journal, match), and replay on restart. The Vision describes the purpose and the roadmap, and the Spec is the source of truth for the code state and the numbered design decisions D1-D77 that later steps cite.

tour.title: Entry Point and Build
tour.description: Main.java is the command-line launcher. It either runs an operator tool (--add-user, --quarantine, --compact) or loads credentials, binds the TCP/TLS gateway and starts the ExchangeService writer, and it maps failures to exit codes 0/1/2 so a halted writer stops the whole process. The Maven pom builds the runnable jar around exchangeserver.Main with no runtime dependencies, and adds the 'bench' (JMH) and 'mutation' (PIT) profiles you will meet at the end of the tour.
tour.languageLesson: Maven profiles (<profile> blocks activated with -P) let one pom define optional build modes. Here -Pbench and -Pmutation add JMH and PIT runs without slowing the default 'test' lifecycle.

tour.title: Domain Vocabulary and Rules
tour.description: Before the engine makes sense you need its vocabulary. Side and OrderType (LIMIT, IOC, FOK, MARKET, POST_ONLY) are the most widely used types in the codebase, OrderRequest is the immutable client order and the only layer of stateless field validation, and Order is an accepted request plus a sequencer-issued id and timestamp. Rules collects every rule that replay depends on, behind a VERSION number that the journal header records, so changing a rule cannot silently change how old history replays.
tour.languageLesson: Java 17 records (record OrderRequest(...)) give immutable value types with a compact constructor where validation runs, so an invalid instance can never exist.

tour.title: The Order Book
tour.description: OrderBook owns every resting order: bid and ask TreeMaps of PriceLevels, an order-id map and per-participant open counts. Each PriceLevel is a time-priority queue built as a sentinel-bounded doubly linked list of OrderNodes, which gives O(1) cancel. All PriceLevel mutators are package-private, so code in other packages (including the engine) can only change the book through add, fillBest and cancel, and those methods keep the invariants in one place. Fill and RestingOrderView report results and expose read-only views without handing out the mutable Order.
tour.languageLesson: Java has no 'friend' classes. Package-private visibility (no modifier) is how this project gets the compiler to enforce ownership: only classes in exchangeserver.book can call PriceLevel's mutators.

tour.title: Price-Time Matching Engine
tour.description: Building on the book from Step 4, MatchingEngine runs side-effect-free pre-checks (duplicate client order id, price band, caps, FOK fillability, post-only), then a shared matching loop with self-trade prevention and per-OrderType outcomes. It is deterministic: it reads no clock, counter or randomness, so feeding it the same commands always produces the same outputs, and replay depends on that. Results come out as sealed EngineOutput records: a Response for the submitter, Trades that carry the incoming command's timestamp, and Reason codes for state-dependent rejects.
tour.languageLesson: A sealed interface (sealed interface EngineOutput permits ...) restricts its implementations to a known set, so the compiler knows every case that code over EngineOutput has to handle.

tour.title: Commands and the Sequencer
tour.description: The engine never sees raw requests. It sees stamped Commands: NEW, CANCEL, CANCEL_ALL, SKIP and CHECK records with a sequence number and a timestamp. The Sequencer is the only component that reads the clock and counts, issuing sequence numbers, order ids and non-decreasing timestamps, which is how the determinism from Step 5 is kept. CheckCommand carries an output digest that replay must reproduce, and SkipCommand quarantines a poison-pill command by adding a note to history instead of editing it.

tour.title: The Write-Ahead Journal
tour.description: Every stamped command is made durable before it is processed. CommandJournal locks the file (JournalLock: one owner at a time), checks the header and Rules.VERSION before changing anything, cuts a torn last record, and appends each batch with one write and one fsync. JournalCodec defines format v3, text records each sealed with a CRC-32C from Checksums, and .gitattributes marks journal files as binary so that git never converts their LF line endings to CRLF.
tour.languageLesson: A write-ahead log only protects you once the data is on disk: forcing the file (fsync) is the step that lets an append survive a power loss. It costs about 1.5 ms on the dev disk, which is why the project batches many commands per fsync.

tour.title: The Exchange Pipeline
tour.description: Exchange.process connects the previous steps: it stamps a batch with the Sequencer, appends it to the CommandJournal with one fsync, feeds each command to the Ledger, calls the OutputListener and only then completes the futures. The Ledger bundles everything derived from commands (the MatchingEngine, the OutputDigest and the per-participant OutputLog) so it can be rebuilt as one unit. OutputDigest is a running FNV-1a hash of every engine output, written into CHECK records, and OutputLog numbers each participant's private events so RESEND works after a restart.

tour.title: Single-Writer Thread Model
tour.description: ExchangeService is how other threads reach the Exchange from Step 8. A caller hands in a Request (Submit, Cancel, CancelAll, or a read such as Snapshot), gets its own CompletableFuture back, and a dedicated 'exchange-writer' thread drains the queue in batches and calls Exchange.process. The state check, the enqueue and stop() share one lock, so no accepted request is ever lost, and ExchangeException tells callers whether to retry (BUSY) or give up (STOPPED, HALTED). Only the writer thread ever touches the book, the engine or the journal.
tour.languageLesson: Completing a CompletableFuture creates a happens-before edge: everything the writer did before completing it is visible to a thread that later reads the result. That is why the tests inspect state only through a future.

tour.title: Recovery: Snapshots and Replay
tour.description: On restart, Replay rebuilds the Ledger in two passes. The first checks sequence and timestamp continuity and collects SKIPs; the second feeds the remaining commands to the same engine and checks every CHECK digest, so a behaviour change in the code shows up as a DIVERGED replay. Snapshot lets recovery start part-way through history from a checksummed '<journal>.snapshot-<seq>' file holding an EngineState, and Durable provides the atomic write-and-rename and directory fsync that make those files crash-safe. ReplayException tells the operator whether a record is a poison pill or a divergence.

tour.title: The TCP/TLS Gateway
tour.description: The gateway is the network edge of the live path. TcpGateway accepts connections (optionally over TLS) and, as the exchange's OutputListener, sends private events to their owners and market data to subscribers. Each ClientSession has a reader thread that authenticates LOGIN against salted PBKDF2 hashes in Credentials, parses lines with Protocol, builds the OrderRequest and applies the in-flight cap and rate limit, so invalid requests are answered with ERROR and never reach the queue. Protocol's header comment is the reference for the wire format.

tour.title: The Client Side
tour.description: To use the gateway from Step 11, ClientMain is an interactive console client: it connects (optionally with a TLS truststore), forwards the protocol lines you type and prints every server line as it arrives. ExchangeClient is the minimal blocking client underneath, with a background reader thread and an await() that finds matching lines. The gateway tests use it too, so it shows how a client is expected to use the protocol.

tour.title: Tests, Seams and Benchmarks
tour.description: There is one test class per production class, with @Nested groups per behaviour. ExchangeServiceTest blocks the writer deterministically with a Gate CommandInterceptor instead of using sleeps, OrderBookTest re-checks the book invariants under randomized traffic, and MutableClock lets tests control the Sequencer's timestamps. MatchingBenchmark measures engine cost from 10 to 100,000 price levels with JMH, and the testing guide explains the seams and the PIT mutation-testing results.
tour.languageLesson: JUnit 5 @Nested inner classes group related tests under one outer class, so test reports show the behaviour group above each test. Mutation testing (PIT) checks how strong the tests are by changing the code and confirming that some test fails.
